title: Eval acceptance thresholds & reporting format — sign-off
summary: Finalize go/no-go thresholds for the 4-week PoC: latency and throughput SLOs, cost guardrails, and a standard benchmark report template. Agree next steps for benchmark runs, security docs, and stakeholder signoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll go for about 45 minutes, objective is final sign-off on acceptance thresholds and the reporting format for the PoC.
[00:10] Anika Rao: Sounds good, thanks Maya. quick context, we want to validate inference end-to-end for our triage assistant prototype — latency, cost, and model quality are the big ones.
[00:25] Carlos Ruiz: Great, can you remind us of target QPS and typical prompt lengths you expect?
[00:30] Tom Jenkins: Typical usage is bursty — 12 to 30 QPS peak per region, median prompt tokens 120, responses usually 70 tokens, but we have longer fallbacks up to 600 in rare flows.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Noted, that distribution matters for batching and cache behavior. For acceptance thresholds we recommended separate buckets: short (<=256) and long (>256) sequences.
[00:55] Ben Carter: For the org to move forward we need a clear go/no-go. What are your suggested thresholds?
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: From an infra perspective we propose: p50 latency < 60ms for short, p95 < 180ms; for long sequences p50 < 220ms p95 < 600ms. Throughput: sustain 25 QPS with < 5% error rate. Cost: average per-request inference cost under $0.035 for the short bucket.
[01:30] Anika Rao: The cost number is critical — how do you compute that? Is that token-based or request-based?
[01:35] Maya Thompson: It's token-normalized using our hosted pricing for the model family that will be used in PoC. For transparency we'll include per-token breakdown and raw token counts in the report.
[01:45] Lina Ortiz: Security: we need data residency and KMS integration. Are audit logs going to be part of the report?
[01:50] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll include a security appendix: SOC2 status, KMS key rotation info, and delivery of audit log snippets. For Private deployments we'll provide a separate checklist.
[02:05] Tom Jenkins: What about fallback behavior — if dedicated capacity isn't available do you fall back to smaller model or different region? We need that in the acceptance tests.
[02:12] Carlos Ruiz: We'll test both: primary path (preferred model, region) and fallback path (compatible model in same region, then cross-region). The PoC acceptance will mark fallback runs separately — they don't count toward pass for primary SLA but are important for reliability metrics.
[02:30] Maya Thompson: On reporting format — we propose a single CSV with row-per-run including fields: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, p50_ms, p95_ms, errors, cost_usd, region, path_taken. Plus a 4-slide PDF summary with charts (latency distributions, cost breakdown, pass/fail table).
[02:50] Ben Carter: Can you show an example of the pass/fail table?
[02:55] Carlos Ruiz: Sure, simplest: rows for each test scenario (short/long/fallback/high-concurrency). Columns: metric, threshold, observed_value, pass(Boolean), notes. We'll attach a template after the call.
[03:10] Anika Rao: For quality, we need an accuracy metric for NLU intents — we'll run 1k labeled prompts and expect >= 92% intent accuracy. How do you capture that in the report?
[03:20] Priya Nair: We'll include an evaluation CSV mapping request_id to expected and predicted label, plus aggregated metrics (accuracy, precision/recall). That will be separate from latency/cost CSV.
[03:35] Tom Jenkins: Timeline check — we already have infra slots in two weeks for benchmark runs. What do you need from us to start?
[03:40] Maya Thompson: We need a small seed dataset, API keys (or VPC access), and alignment on final test matrix — we've drafted it and will share. Runs will take ~48 hours to complete, then 3 days to analyze + reporting. So 4-week total from kickoff to sign-off sounds right.
[04:00] Ben Carter: Who signs off at the end? We want a single gate.
[04:05] Maya Thompson: Proposed: Anika signs on product/quality and Lina signs on security. Redwood will provide the benchmark report and call a review meeting; both signatures required for go.
[04:18] Anika Rao: Works for me.
[04:20] Lina Ortiz: Same, assuming security appendix meets our checklist.
[04:25] Carlos Ruiz: Quick note on load generation — we'll run both synthetic and production-capture replay. Synthetic runs will test steady-state and spikes; replay will test real prompt distributions. We'll tag rows in the CSV with run_type.
[04:42] Tom Jenkins: Are regression alerts part of the acceptance criteria? Like model output degradation?
[04:45] Priya Nair: Not for the initial pass, but we'll include automatic quality monitors and a fail-if-drop>3% vs baseline in a secondary gating. Primary go focuses on latency/cost/accuracy thresholds defined.
[05:00] Ben Carter: Ok let's state concrete go/no-go rules on record:
[05:05] Maya Thompson: Reading: 1) Primary path short bucket: p95 < 180ms AND avg cost/request <= $0.035. 2) Long bucket primary path: p95 < 600ms AND no data loss, error rate < 1.5%. 3) Quality: labeled intent accuracy >= 92% on the 1k sample. 4) Throughput: sustain 25 QPS with <5% errors. If all four true => GO. If any single primary fails => NO-GO (but we provide remediation plan). Fallback path performance and security appendix do not veto but must be delivered.
[05:40] Anika Rao: Agreed.
[05:42] Lina Ortiz: Agreed pending KMS integration docs.
[05:45] Carlos Ruiz: We'll put pass/fail flags in the CSV and the PDF will include a checklist per rule.
[05:55] Ben Carter: Let's lock down dates — can we schedule the benchmark kickoff next Monday?
[06:00] Maya Thompson: We can, assuming you give the seed data and VPC access by Thursday COB. That aligns with the 4-week end date: sign-off meeting Apr 14th.
[06:10] Tom Jenkins: We'll aim for Thursday.
[06:12] Maya Thompson: Great. Any other items?
[06:14] Anika Rao: One question on competitors — you mentioned vendor comparatives earlier, can you include an appendix comparing latency/cost vs Anthropic and OpenAI baselines?
[06:20] Priya Nair: We can include non-production comparative runs if you authorize the benchmark. We'll note differences in model families.
[06:28] Ben Carter: Okay. Thanks everyone.
[06:30] Maya Thompson: Recap: Maya will send the test matrix and CSV + PDF templates, Redwood SE to run benchmarks, customer to provide seed dataset, VPC/API access, and security contacts. Signoff rules are the four items stated. Meeting adjourned.
[06:45] (end)
